original_test_intent: Complete exactly 100 physical tray AC cycles and show reliable recovery with stable OS, PCIe, MCTP and the engineering-resolved SSIF/FPGA/SMA health set on every cycle.
original_method: An authorized electrical/hardware operator uses the approved tray feed procedure for all 100 cycles, with exact counter, dwell and physical evidence; an independent console/evidence collector verifies boot and the resolved endpoint matrix after each restoration, halting on the first unsafe anomaly.
manual_activity: An authorized operator physically removes and restores the exact tray AC feed for cycles 1-100, records every action and pauses permanently on unsafe power, connector or recovery behavior pending owner review.
required_inputs: Approved Vera Rubin NVL72 validation-guide revision replacing NVOnline TBD
Decision whether required stability covers SSIF, FPGA, SMA or all three and exact acceptance for each
Tray/PSU/feed/PDU/outlet/connector map and complete AC/aux boundary
100-cycle counter, off dwell, discharge/inrush, POST/OS timeout and resume policy
Workload drain, storage flush, data and maintenance-window approval
Expected PCIe devices/links, MCTP endpoints/EIDs/routes and resolved SSIF/FPGA/SMA matrix
Independent console/power observer, artifact storage and recovery
safety_requirements: Never automate or delegate unlabeled connector/feed operations to an agent
Do not reduce the 100-cycle denominator or treat a smoke sample as completion
Do not continue after arcing, connector/PSU damage, abnormal inrush or incomplete AC boundary
Persist cycle index/evidence atomically and preserve the first failed state
Stop on boot timeout, missing/downtrained PCIe, MCTP or resolved endpoint mismatch, AER/DPC, storage/data, thermal/power or recovery fault
No automatic retry or silent cycle replacement
agent_execution_scope: Verify guide, resolved health matrix and approved physical plan
Collect comprehensive read-only baseline and prepare cycle ledger
After operator actions, collect per-cycle OS/PCIe/MCTP/resolved endpoint and error/health evidence
Perform no physical AC action, PDU control, retry, conflict resolution, workload restore or verdict
engineer_actions: Resolve SSIF/FPGA versus SMA and supply guide revision
Approve exact physical AC boundary, 100-cycle safety/timing and recovery
Define per-interface identity/health/error criteria and denominator
Review first failure and all 100 results and issue PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED

modernized_recommendation.status: MANUAL CRITICAL 100-CYCLE AC ENDURANCE PENDING HEALTH-MATRIX DECISION
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Maintain a tamper-evident cycle ledger binding each physical feed event to console/boot and normalized OS/PCIe/MCTP/resolved SSIF-FPGA-SMA evidence, with mandatory stop on first anomaly.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds exact power boundary, guide/criteria decision, electrical controls, durable cycle accounting and full post-cycle evidence without automating the physical bench action.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Warm or BMC DC stress cannot replace physical AC loss. SMA evidence cannot silently stand for SSIF/FPGA, and a reduced cycle sample cannot establish 100-cycle endurance.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Repeated connector/service operations create cumulative mechanical and inrush risk, while intermittent platform failures can disappear after another cycle. The first abnormal physical or logical state must be preserved instead of retried away.

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Procedure requires SSIF and FPGA stability, while Criteria replaces those with SMA stability; the referenced Vera Rubin guide is TBD. These interfaces cannot be assumed equivalent or silently merged.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The physical 100-cycle AC purpose is clear and reviewable. Execution may be prepared while final acceptance waits for the health-matrix decision and approved guide.

engineering_decision_pending: Resolve Functionality row 1927 Wistron-GB NV PVP HW-00010-V002: provide the approved Vera Rubin NVL72 guide and decide whether all 100 AC cycles require SSIF, FPGA, SMA or all three; define exact per-cycle identities/health limits, physical AC boundary, stop/resume and recovery while preserving every named source field.
review_improvement: Preserves all 100 operator-owned AC events, exposes the SSIF/FPGA/SMA mismatch and adds durable physical/logical evidence and safety stop controls.
independent_technical_reasoning: SSIF, FPGA health and SMA are different interfaces or components with different failure modes, so substituting one for another would erase coverage. Physical AC endurance also measures cumulative power-path and initialization reliability; each cycle must remain individually attributable. A ledger linking the feed event to endpoint state prevents a generic successful boot from hiding partial recovery or an unperformed cycle.
